definitions.explanation: Polite term used to refer to another person's husband. The honorific ご makes it respectful.
Can also refer to the master of a house or the proprietor of a shop.

examples.japanese: ご{主人|しゅじん}はお{元気|げんき}ですか。
ご{主人|しゅじん}のお{仕事|しごと}は{何|なん}ですか。
examples.english: What does your husband do for work?

examples.japanese: このお{店|みせ}のご{主人|しゅじん}は{親切|しんせつ}だ。
examples.english: The owner of this shop is kind.

examples.japanese: ご{主人|しゅじん}にもよろしくお{伝|つた}えください。
examples.english: Please give my regards to your husband.

examples.japanese: ご{主人|しゅじん}と{一緒|いっしょ}に{来|こ}られますか。
examples.english: Will you come with your husband?

examples.japanese: この{旅館|りょかん}のご{主人|しゅじん}は{料理|りょうり}が{上手|じょうず}だ。
examples.english: The proprietor of this inn is good at cooking.

examples.japanese: ご{主人|しゅじん}がいらっしゃらないときは、お{電話|でんわ}いたします。
examples.english: I will call when your husband is home.

examples.japanese: {居酒屋|いざかや}のご{主人|しゅじん}に{おすすめ|おすすめ}を{聞|き}いた。
examples.english: I asked the owner of the izakaya for recommendations.

examples.japanese: ご{主人|しゅじん}のご{趣味|しゅみ}は{何|なん}ですか。
この{老舗|しにせ}のご{主人|しゅじん}は{三代目|さんだいめ}で、{祖父|そふ}の{代|だい}からの{伝統|でんとう}を{守|まも}り{続|つづ}けているそうだ。
examples.english: The owner of this long-established shop is the third generation, and I hear he continues to preserve the traditions from his grandfather's time.

notes:
ご{主人|しゅじん} is the polite form for referring to someone else's husband.

RELATED TERMS:
- {主人|しゅじん}: my husband (humble when referring to own spouse)
- {夫|おっと}: husband (neutral/formal for own husband)
- {旦那|だんな}さん: husband (casual-polite for someone else's)
- {奥|おく}さん: (someone else's) wife

USAGE NOTE: Using {主人|しゅじん} for one's own husband is traditional but some consider it old-fashioned. Modern alternatives include {夫|おっと} or パートナー.

[Register: Polite]
